2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 19.8649%, with a VOC of 1.1152 V, FF of 76.5855%, and JSC of 23.259 mA/cm². A solution of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 at 1.5 mol/L provided the foundational matrix for the perovskite layer. For the perovskite films, the spin-coating process was divided into a consecutive two-step procedure: the spin rate of the first step was 1200 rpm for 10 s, and that of the second step was 5000 rpm for 30 s. 200 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate at the last 8 s of the spin-coating, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation (Cs⁺/FA⁺) that enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation through an optimized Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), a Pb²⁺ B-site enabling strong spin–orbit coupling and suitable bandgap tuning (~1.58 eV), and a mixed I⁻/Br⁻ X-site that modulates lattice strain while mitigating halide segregation—undergoes highly controlled crystallization via a two-step spin-coating protocol wherein the initial low-speed (1200 rpm, 10 s) step ensures uniform precursor wetting and nucleation site distribution, while the subsequent high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) step governs solvent evaporation kinetics and film thinning; critically, the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 200 µL chlorobenzene at the final 8 s triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting rapid nucleation of small, energetically favorable crystallites that evolve during thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min into large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain defect density and suppressed ion migration pathways—evidenced by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, confirming high crystallinity and minimal microstrain, while PL mapping reveals spatially homogeneous intensity and a monoexponential decay with τₐᵥₑ ≈ 385 ns, indicating uniform radiative recombination and low non-radiative trap density across the film; optical microscopy and grayscale-integrated film coverage analysis further corroborate near-unity surface continuity (>99.2% coverage) with negligible pinholes or dewetting features, collectively ensuring unimpeded vertical charge transport and minimized interfacial recombination at both electron- and hole-selective contacts—thereby enabling VOC of 1.1152 V, JSC of 23.259 mA/cm², FF of 76.5855%, and PCE of 19.8649%.
